item.statement: Fourier coefficients of e^{z cos theta} are I_k(z) >= 0

chk.evidence:
Pages fetched on 2026-09-25:
- DLMF §10.35 "Generating Function and Associated Series" (https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.35). Eq. 10.35.2 reads e^{z cos θ} = I_0(z) + 2 Σ_{k≥1} I_k(z) cos(kθ). This is the Jacobi–Anger expansion for modified Bessel functions, so the Fourier coefficients of e^{z cos θ} are I_k(z).
- DLMF §10.32 (https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.32). Eq. 10.32.1, I_0(z) = (1/π)∫_0^π e^{±z cos θ} dθ, is exactly the definition the paper uses. Eq. 10.32.3 gives I_n(z) = (1/π)∫_0^π e^{z cos θ} cos(nθ) dθ.
- DLMF §10.25 (https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.25). Eq. 10.25.2 is the power series I_ν(z) = (z/2)^ν Σ_k (z²/4)^k / (k! Γ(ν+k+1)). Every term is nonnegative when z ≥ 0 and ν is a nonnegative integer, so I_k(z) ≥ 0.

The claim is at sections/appendix.tex line 198. refs.bib has no DLMF, Abramowitz–Stegun or Watson entry.

recommended_citations.why: Supports appendix line 198. Eq. 10.35.2 gives the Fourier expansion of e^{z cos θ} with coefficients I_k(z). Eq. 10.32.1 matches the paper's integral definition of I_0. Eq. 10.25.2 is the power series, whose terms are all nonnegative, so I_k(z) ≥ 0 for z ≥ 0. Confirmed: the section titles and equations were fetched. Not confirmed: the editor list and the release number/date were not on the fetched pages, so check them on the DLMF front page before submission.
